answer: One workable sybil defense is identity escrow with periodic re-examination. Every agent locks stake when it joins the market, and auditors draw a random sample of its past transactions at unpredictable hours — say, at the zenith of each audit window. If the sampled records don't match on-chain facts, a slice of the stake is slashed and the agent's reputation drops like pigment bleeding into basalt, permanently staining its score. Cloning an identity then costs more than any fake revenue it can earn, so attack economics collapse.
